svg.title: AfterWard at scale
svg.text: WHAT'S NEXT · TARGET ARCHITECTURE · DATA STAYS IN THE EU
AfterWard at scale: built for millions of patients
Same MCP tools and safety gate as today. Amber boxes are new.
AfterWard MCP server · same 9 tools as today
ECS Fargate across 3 Availability Zones, behind a load balancer
Stateless, so it auto-scales: more tasks at 8 am, fewer at night
Crisis check first; Bedrock Guardrails on every model reply
Bedrock Claude for our app's agent; Alexa+ users bring their own
Model calls use EU cross-region inference to spread the load
so most reads skip the database
by patient; scales on its own
Object Lock for the audit copy
AWS Step Functions: the letter pipeline
1 Amazon Textract reads scans and photos; pypdf reads text PDFs
2 Bedrock Claude fills the fixed form (batch mode when it can wait)
4 Anything flagged goes to a clinician review queue (Amazon A2I)
5 Save the plan; chunk, embed and index the letter
Each step retries on its own; one slow letter never blocks others
app push or SMS, by the
dose time, made from the plan;
Reserved concurrency smooths the 8 am peak
Checks the plan first: no reminder for a dose already taken
Sends by Amazon SNS / End User Messaging (push, SMS)
Reminder text built by code, not the model
Warning signs and missed doses raise an alert (SQS + SNS)
Clinicians confirm flagged items from the letter pipeline
Every confirmation is logged in the patient's history
AfterWard supports the care team; it never replaces it

g.text: ~6 MCP tool calls a day each → 6 million a day: ~70 a second on average, ~700 at the 8 am peak
~4 reminders a day each → 4 million scheduled sends a day, spread across time slots
~30,000 new letters a day → queued and processed in parallel; batch mode when not urgent
Today's measured cost → one letter used ~7,400 tokens in and ~2,700 out (CloudWatch)

svg.text: Design rules that let it grow

g.text: no table has a hot spot
spikes wait in line, nothing is lost
the safety gate scales with review
Same MCP tools at any size
today's code is the core, not a throwaway

svg.text: AfterWard · A living recovery plan for Alexa+
Target design for discussion · Not a medical device · Synthetic data today
